problem: RGB-only zero-shot ObjectNav lacks explicit depth, causing physical uncertainty (scale/distance ambiguity) and semantic-physical misalignment. Semantic/MLLM methods lack geometric grounding, and end-to-end policies lack explicit physical constraints, giving plausible but unsafe behavior.
motivation: Depth-free navigation lowers hardware cost and demands stronger visual reasoning. A unified representation aligning discrete semantic reasoning with continuous physical boundaries is missing. Recent 3D foundation models (VGGT) can recover pseudo-depth and scale from monocular sequences, which suggests occupancy can be reconstructed geometrically.
key_idea: Lift monocular RGB sequences with VGGT and Grounded-SAM into a persistent 3D oriented-bounding-box semantic list, then fuse VLM semantic scores, directional bias and traversability multiplicatively into a Multi-layer Value Map for goal selection and A*/FMM planning.
insight: Explicit 3D structure from a foundation model plus a multiplicative cost space lets an RGB-only agent match or exceed some RGB-D zero-shot methods. Ablations show explore memory (SR 65.4→38.2) and VLM rating (→45.7) matter most. Removing semantic floor re-projection raises SPL (27.9→30.5) but lowers SR (→53.2), so it trades efficiency for safety. Full-sequence reconstruction runs out of memory, which motivates the recursive stage-wise reconstruction (~30 images per stage).
method: Physical Perception: VGGT is run on ~30 images per stage to regress pseudo-depth and camera parameters, and pixels are back-projected to a point cloud. Grounded-SAM produces target, general-object and floor masks; non-floor BEV occupancy is inflated into a local occupancy map.

Global Spatial Semantic List (GSSL): point clusters of target and general objects are fitted separately with 3D OBBs. Labels are set by majority vote, and an entity must be seen in at least 3 frames. VGGT trajectory is aligned to metric odometry by a similarity transform (σ,R,t). Entities are fused across stages by 3D IoU.

VLM High-level Reasoning: GPT-4o-mini scores each newly detected GSSL entity in [0,1] with common-sense priors. It picks a mode: Explore (coarse direction), Find (go to target or strong cue), or Judge (verify the goal).

Multi-layer Value Map: Φ_total = Φ_sem ⊙ Φ_dir ⊙ Φ_trav. Φ_sem is a clipped sum of Gaussians weighted by VLM scores, Φ_dir is a forward-semicircle angular Gaussian, and Φ_trav = 1−exp(−k·d_min). The midterm goal is the argmax of Φ_total.

Low-level Execution: A* on the local occupancy map, plus a sliding-window FMM giving short-term goals. A safety layer re-projects the short-term goal onto the floor mask and rotates if it falls outside. VLM inference for the next stage is overlapped with movement once within 3 m of the goal.

Episode start/finish: the goal image is parsed into main and sub targets, and the agent does an initial 360° scan. In Judge mode it does a 360° scan, matches views with LightGlue, and a VLM confirms the target before STOP.

setting.observation: monocular RGB 640x480 plus pose (localization/odometry); no depth
setting.simulator: Habitat (HM3D, MP3D, RoboTHOR) plus real robot
setting.privileged: Ground-truth/onboard pose provided; the goal image is taken from the episode file

numbers.extra: RGB-only, training-free; goal image from episode

numbers_note: Split names are the paper's 'validation episodes'; mapped to 'val'. Real-world results are in a table of 40 trials per scene (not simulation benchmark).
results: Training-free RGB-only MVP-Nav reaches HM3D SR 65.4/SPL 27.9, beating the RGB baseline PanoNav (43.5/23.7) and RGB-D SG-Nav (54.0/24.9) and UniGoal (54.5/25.1) in SR. On MP3D it gets 50.4/18.1 and on RoboTHOR 57.5/26.8. Real-robot success was 45.0% (18/40) in the corridor and 47.5% (19/40) in the office.
limitations: Long-range monocular depth (e.g. a 60 m corridor) causes point cloud drift and low real-world success (35–60%).
High latency: ~13 s per stage from perception plus API-based VLM, only hidden by pipelining; VGGT needs ~15.7 GB VRAM and long sequences run out of memory.
Relies on given pose/odometry and a goal image, and depends on a closed API VLM.
